steps.title: Lesson 2: Core Concepts
steps.body: Key Fact: Always write answers in the context of the question: if the data is about rainfall, say ‘rainfall’ not ‘the data’ or ‘the values’ | Key Fact: Support every statement with a specific data value: ‘The median rainfall in July (68 mm) was higher than in April (42 mm)’ | Key Fact: Avoid vague language: replace ‘quite high’, ‘bigger’, ‘a lot’ with precise values and comparisons | Key Fact: When comparing distributions, always compare both location (median/mean) AND spread (IQR/range/SD)
